title: Dujmović–Joret–Morin–Norin–Wood Question on 2-tree-width and chromatic number
statement_text: There exists a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that every graph $G$ with 2-tree-width at most $k$ has chromatic number at most $f(k)$.
context_text: The authors of [5] asked whether $\chi(G)$ is bounded from above by a function of the 2-tree-width of $G$, motivated by the fact that this holds for 2-path-width (via the Asplund–Grünbaum theorem on rectangle intersection graphs). The present paper provides a negative answer, showing triangle-free Burling graphs with arbitrarily large chromatic number have 2-tree-width (and even mixed tree/path-decomposition width) at most 2.
attributed_to: Dujmović, Joret, Morin, Norin, and Wood
paper_contribution: Disproves the question by constructing, for every $k \geq 1$, a Burling graph $G_k$ with a tree-decomposition and a path-decomposition such that each bag of the first intersects each bag of the second in at most 2 vertices, while $\chi(G_k) \geq k$.
paper_title: Burling graphs, chromatic number, and orthogonal tree-decompositions

title: Conjecture 3
statement_text: There exists a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that $\chi(G) \leq f(k)$ for every $k \geq 1$ and every graph $G$ admitting a spaghetti tree-decomposition $(T, \{B_t\}_{t \in V(T)})$ and a path-decomposition $(P, \{B_p\}_{p \in V(P)})$ such that $|B_t \cap B_p| \leq k$ for every $t \in V(T)$ and $p \in V(P)$.
context_text: A tree-decomposition $(T,\{B_t\}_{t\in V(T)})$ of $G$ (with bags $B_t\subseteq V(G)$) is a spaghetti tree-decomposition if $T$ is rooted at some vertex $r$ and, orienting all edges of $T$ away from $r$, the subtree $T_v$ of $T$ induced by $\{t\in V(T): v\in B_t\}$ is a directed path for each vertex $v$ of $G$; a path-decomposition is a tree-decomposition whose tree is a path. Motivation: a classic result of Asplund and Grünbaum states that intersection graphs of axis-aligned rectangles in the plane are $\chi$-bounded (here $\chi(G)\in O(\omega(G)^2)$); equivalently, there is a function $f$ such that every graph having two path-decompositions in which each bag of the first meets each bag of the second in at most $k$ vertices has chromatic number at most $f(k)$. Dujmović, Joret, Morin, Norin and Wood asked whether this remains true for two tree-decompositions. The authors answer this negatively: the Burling graphs (triangle-free with unbounded chromatic number) admit a tree-decomposition and a path-decomposition such that every bag of the first meets every bag of the second in at most two vertices. The conjecture, posed as an open problem in the spirit of extending the Asplund–Grünbaum result, asks whether restricting the tree-decomposition to be a spaghetti one restores a bound. The authors remark that, for all they know, it could even hold with two spaghetti tree-decompositions; graphs having a spaghetti tree-decomposition where $uv\in E(G)$ if and only if $T_u$ and $T_v$ intersect (a subclass of chordal graphs) were studied by Galvin.
paper_title: Burling graphs, chromatic number, and orthogonal tree-decompositions
